newsitem.title: USA: Clinton lawyer seeks delay in sex-harassment case.
newsitem.headline: Clinton lawyer seeks delay in sex-harassment case.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's lawyer asked the Supreme Court on Monday to give Clinton temporary immunity from civil lawsuits and delay a sex-harassment case until after he leaves office in 2001.

"Here you have a sitting president. We are saying we will give Miss Jones her day in court. Let's not do it now," Clinton lawyer Robert Bennett said of the sexual harassment case filed by former Arkansas state employee Paula Jones for an incident she alleges happened in 1991 when he was Arkansas governor.

Clinton's position was backed by a top Justice Department lawyer, Acting Solicitor General Walter Dellinger, who said an incumbent president should not be distracted from the demands of the office by having to appear in court.

But Gilbert Davis, an attorney for Jones, said the lawsuit -- alleging Clinton made unwanted sexual advances to Jones in a Little Rock hotel room in 1991, when she was working at an Arkansas government conference -- should be allowed to go forward now.

He argued that Jones wants to restore her reputation, and said witnesses could die, their memories could fade and documents could be lost if the case were postponed until Clinton no longer was president. He will be inaugurated for a second four-year term next Monday and would leave office four years from that day.

The Supreme Court justices vigorously questioned all of the lawyers during the hour-long arguments, but gave no firm indication of how they would rule. A decision in the closely watched case is due by the end of June.
